newsitem.title: USA: U.S. criticizes Israeli road-building project.
newsitem.headline: U.S. criticizes Israeli road-building project.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday criticised an Israeli government move to press ahead with a road-building project around Jerusalem, saying it would not create confidence with the Palestinians.
Israeli ministers agreed Tuesday to speed building of roads in and around Arab East Jerusalem, which Palestinians want to make the capital of a future state.
"We would have preferred that the action just taken by the Israeli government not have been taken at this time," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said.

"We've said to both parties since the Hebron agreement that they should act in ways which build confidence and enhance prospects for future progress," he told a news briefing. "We would prefer to see steps taken now which continue to build positive momentum."

Under the Jan. 15 Hebron deal, Israel agreed to hand over 80 percent of the West Bank city to Palestinian control. It was the last of seven West Bank towns from which Israel redeployed troops under a 1995 accord.
Davies noted that the road project was originally approved by the former Labour government of Yitzhak Rabin with the aim of relieving congestion. Rabin was assassinated in 1995.

Despite the road-building decision, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Tuesday postponed debate for at least a week on another controversial project, to build on a forested hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem in the West Bank.
Davies declined comment on the so-called Har Homa project, which opponents say could lead to a new upsurge of Palestinian anger and possible violence.
